scenes.text: In episode 11, we learned that MCP is like a USB-C port for AI, one standard way to plug in tools. [1] Today, we build our own MCP server, a notes app any AI assistant can use. [2] About fifteen lines of Python.

title: Build an
MCP Server
data.subtitle: Plug your tools into any AI

scenes.text: Here's how the pieces fit. [1] The user chats in an AI app, like Claude Desktop, or an IDE. [2] The app has a built-in MCP client. [3] The client connects to our MCP server. [4] The server offers tools, like add note, and list notes. [5] The model calls them, whenever it needs to.

Why not just put tools inside your app, like last episode? [1] Tools in your code work only in your own app. [2] An MCP server works with any MCP-compatible app. Build it once, and plug it in everywhere.

[1] Here's the server, using the official Python SDK. Install it with pip install mcp. [2] Import FastMCP. [3] Create a server called notes, and a list to hold them. [4] Now, a tool. The decorator registers it, and the type hints, and docstring, tell the AI what it does, and what inputs it takes. This one saves a note. [5] A second tool returns all the notes. [6] Finally, run the server. [7] Connect it to an app, and just ask in plain English!

data.heading: A notes MCP server
output: $ claude mcp add notes -- python notes.py

scenes.text: Here are four terms. [1] MCP server, a program that offers tools to AI apps. [2] MCP client, the part of the AI app that connects to servers. [3] Resource, read-only data a server can share, like files. [4] And transport, how they talk. Local servers usually use standard input and output.

What could you build? [1] A server for your company's database, so AI can answer sales questions. [2] A server for your smart home, to switch lights on and off. [3] Or a server for your college timetable, and assignments.

Here's an important warning. [1] People install any MCP server they find online. [2] A server can run code on your computer, and read your data. Only install servers from sources you trust, and give them the least access they need.

data.myth: Any MCP server from the internet is safe to install.
data.fact: Servers can run code and read your data. Use trusted sources and least access.

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] An MCP server offers tools to any MCP app. [2] FastMCP turns Python functions into tools, with one decorator. [3] Docstrings and type hints describe them to the AI. [4] And only install servers you trust. [5] Next, build a voice assistant. Follow AI Maastaaru!
